crime: {WITCH_NAME} and another prisoner became confidantes in prison. They traded one private worry at a time and gave each other private advice. {WITCH_NAME} once sent the girl a phone photo of a handwritten confession about someone she loved. The girl forwarded it to a small prison group chat, then claimed every copy had been deleted.

During afternoon free time, {WITCH_NAME} watched the girl take an ordinary book from a low shelf in the library. The girl showed another prisoner the saved confession photo, said she would forward it again after dinner, and pointed out the book she planned to return and finish that evening. She heard the promise and saw exactly where the book belonged.

After dinner, the girl returned to the library while several prisoners read nearby. The girl crouched and pulled out the book she had named. A short loop hidden behind the spines drew a second hardback down from above it. The nearby readers saw the hardback strike the girl's head without anyone touching it during the fall. The girl died immediately. The short drop left a deep rectangular depression in the victim's skull that matched the book's corner. That corner was crushed and bloodied.

A narrow strip from {WITCH_NAME}'s distinctive cuff was pinched beneath the hidden loop's knot, and the cuff had a matching fresh tear. {WITCH_NAME} admitted reshelving the hardback and snagging her cuff there, but called the death an accident and denied using magic.

The readers' account ruled out an attacker at the moment of death. The hardback had fallen too short a distance to cause such a fracture by its own weight, while its damaged, bloodied corner proved it had delivered the fatal blow. The hidden loop made the fall deliberate. The cloth trapped beneath its knot proved she had tied the loop, not merely shelved the book. Her account could explain the torn cuff, but not the loop or the impossible force.

In the empty lounge, {WITCH_NAME} had swung the flat of a sword into one palm. That palm received the blow without taking its impact. After returning the sword, she carried the hardback to the library with her free hand, tied the loop, arranged both books, then pressed her other palm to the solid hardback and sealed the same impact inside it. When the victim pulled the lower book, the hardback fell; its strike against the victim's skull was its next collision, so the sealed sword blow released through the hardback and killed her. The witnessed fall, the cloth beneath the knot, and the force only Impact Relay could supply identified her as the person who prepared the trap.
fields.epitaph: One secret left her hands and returned in every mouth.
execution: One enormous iron hand rises from the execution stand. Its palm closes against her back, and its fingers close over her chest and upper arms. The grip pins both arms to her sides and lifts her clear of the stand.

The hand turns its palm outward, holding her exposed before the other prisoners. Its fingers keep closing around her rib cage. Her ribs break inward, her chest collapses, and the hand continues crushing until she can no longer breathe and dies.

magic.name: Impact Relay
magic.text: She can transfer a received impact into another object.
